source.prompt: A California vole (Microtus californicus), a wild meadow vole, NOT a mouse, NOT a hamster. One adult on all fours in a neutral side-on pose, feet on the ground, head level. Realistic proportions: 17 cm long including a short 4.5 cm tail, stocky cylindrical body, short legs, blunt rounded face, small beady eyes, small round ears almost hidden in fur. Grizzled cinnamon-brown back with darker ticking, grey belly, grey feet, tail dark above and grey below. No whiskers as strands. No base, no ground. Game-ready.

accuracy_notes: Generated (one meshy-6-lite preview). Reads as a stocky short-legged vole rather than a mouse once rebuilt: tail cut to 4.5 cm (a quarter of the length) and thickened, ears pressed down 0.6x into the fur, muzzle 0.85x blunter, body 0.85x lower; grizzled brown back with a reddish midline, blue-grey belly, grey feet, tail dark above and grey below. Still wrong or unchecked: the head keeps some of the generator's rat shape (muzzle a little pointed); the thickened tail decimates to a flat blade; the eye is one dark triangle, large for a beady eye at arm's length; lod2 is a 23-triangle wedge; the back is higher than the brief's 4 cm estimate.
